summary: This polymer plant released about 13,600 lb to the air in 2024, almost all methanol, plus a small amount to water.

impacts.title: Air & breathing
impacts.where: Within 1 mile: 3,952 residents; Horace Mann Middle School
impacts.how: About 13,600 lb of methanol went out the stack. At high levels methanol can cause headaches and dizziness. Small amounts of maleic anhydride, which can sensitize the lungs, were also released.

avoid.label: Report odors
avoid.text: Report strong or unusual odors in the forum, where the company can reply. You can also call the DNR tip line, 1-800-847-9367

avoid.label: Check air quality
avoid.text: Check the daily air quality index (AirNow), especially on hot, still days

avoid.label: Ask about permits
avoid.text: Ask the DNR whether the plant's methanol is covered by an air permit

impacts.title: Smog
impacts.how: Methanol helps form ground-level ozone, and Sheboygan's lakeshore doesn't meet the federal ozone standard.

avoid.label: Exercise in the morning
avoid.text: Plan outdoor exercise for mornings on hot, sunny days

avoid.label: Drive less
avoid.text: Drive less on ozone action days

avoid.label: Keep an inhaler handy
avoid.text: Keep rescue inhalers handy on high-ozone days

impacts.title: Sheboygan River
impacts.how: About 15 lb reached water: 5 lb each of antimony, zinc and maleic anhydride. That's small, and these aren't the river's main problem: older PCB pollution is why the DNR still says not to eat resident fish from the lower 14 miles of the river.

avoid.label: Skip river fish
avoid.text: Don't eat resident fish from the lower 14 miles of the Sheboygan River

avoid.label: Check fish advice
avoid.text: Follow the DNR fish advisory for other catches

avoid.label: Keep drains clear
avoid.text: Keep stormwater drains clear of trash and chemicals
